metadata.topic: Evolution of Loop Dynamics, Counter Architecture, and Prog End

context: Discussion originated from the 8-bit sub-operand limitation of the Loop command. It evolved into a major architectural refinement, decoupling immediate execution from queued execution, and transitioning to an up-count architecture.

fixed.description: Repurpose D16-D31 in Global commands into Mode (D28-D31) and secondary sub-operands, enabling Base-Set-free local loops and 20-bit large loops.
Consolidate to a single primary loop counter due to the adoption of an external stack for auto-nesting.
Transition to an up-count system from 0, with automatic clear to 0 upon reaching the target value.
Expose 1-clock match flags (loop_cnt_match, stay_cnt_match, prescaler_match) to external logic for hardware optimization.
Introduce 'Prog End' command. Commands between Stay Set and Prog End are executed immediately (forward-scheduled). Commands after Prog End are queued (backward-scheduled at Timeup).

deferred_ties.description: Prescaler evaluation timing: Leading edge vs Trailing edge for queued executions.
Exact execution timing and semantics of 'Stay Set' (whether it should only be a pre-clear/sync command to avoid jitter).
Necessity of a 'Local Branch' (zero-time-axis-cost conditional branch) for immediate background execution blocks.
Potential of queued 'NOP' as a Timeup-tracking timing placeholder.
Final reassignment of internal control sub-opcodes 0-7 to accommodate Prog End and Local Branch.
